title: N3E_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS and REALM_EDGE_TRUSTED_CIDRS with IPv4-mapped IPv6: the server keeps a mapped address's v6 prefix after canonicalising it to IPv4, so 32 - bits wraps in release builds (overflow-checks off) and the mask becomes 0, trusting every IPv4 peer; a bare ::ffff:a.b.c.d (prefix 128) triggers it as well as /104 (server/src/admission.rs:80-104). realm-edge's saturating_sub(96) turns ::ffff:x/80 into IPv4 /0 (edge/src/config.rs:106). In both, subtract 96 from a mapped prefix and refuse one under 96; unit tests in both crates and a connections_live case. Security.

tests/moradon_skeletal_plug_live.py:194 asserts the glow2233 package's recipe is engine 39, but M4c (854c5f5) made ko_bake.py:462 raise every --features package to engine 42, so the suite has failed since M4c; nobody saw it because it needs the 2145 installer and the operator's MAGIC_TYPE2 export, which this checkout lacked until 2026-11-01 (now linked read-only from the n3e checkout's build/). Fix the assertion to the rule the bake actually applies (and say why), check the suite's other expectations against M4c, run it alone with make live-ko LIVE_KO_SUITES=moradon_skeletal_plug_live, and confirm the other two 2145 suites (moradon_glow_live, moradon_armour_live) still pass.

The maintainer wants to play the game on this machine while the loop runs. Live suites already render offscreen with their own HOME and ports, so what is left is CPU and GPU contention. (1) Run make live once with a real client playing the hosted realm and record which suites, if any, fail or slow down. (2) The gate notes in its log when a game client (not a test client) is running, so a failure is judged with that in mind. (3) If (1) shows suites that cannot share the machine, a PLAYING line in INBOX makes the loop pick items that need no make live until it is removed. Update LOOP.md to match.

Close tools/loop/gate.py's blind spots from review 2026-11-01 section 6 (the maintainer asked for this, 2026-11-01): (1) live suites and shared harnesses without _live in the name trigger make live; (2) KO suites, client/harness/front_end_flow.inc and tools/assetc/moradon_*.py trigger make live-ko; (3) cargo test -p n3e-server also runs for protocol/wire.proto, deploy/*.sql, the server's fixtures, bot/src/admin.rs and rust-toolchain.toml; (4) the gate clears LIVE_SUITES, LIVE_KO_SUITES, LIVE_TICK_MS and LIVE_DISPLAY from the environment it passes on; (5) a SKIP in make test for a fixture this checkout should have fails the gate (LOOP.md: a missing fixture is never a pass), with a short allow-list for inputs only the maintainer holds; (6) flake attribution uses a suite's covers, not tests/<name>.py; (7) content/ and tools/loop/ are not docs. Tests for the step planner (gate.py plan on synthetic change lists). Update LOOP.md's Gate section to match. (8) The gate sources tools/env.sh itself (the pinned toolchain and ImGui): a run from a shell without it failed make live at once on 2026-11-01. (9) Split the gate (the maintainer asked, 2026-11-01, so the loop pauses less): per item, the fast checks (queue, fmt/clippy/test per touched crate, make test) plus only the live and live-ko suites whose covers the change touches; once a day before the push, a full make live and make live-ko on master. A daily failure blocks the push, is attributed to the day's commits (rerun alone once to tell a flake), and files fix items at the top of the queue; never a reset or revert. Steps that are slow and catch little per item move to the daily run by the same rule. Update LOOP.md's Gate section and the skill's daily-push step to match.

Pre-auth slots are held with no time limit after the Handshake: the idle deadline ends at the first frame and any frame (a Ping) resets the 2 s read deadline (server/src/network.rs:266-289, 508-510, 816), so 6 sources at 3 sockets each hold all 16 slots for as long as they like. Bound accept-to-login (a login deadline and a cap on failed login attempts per socket), close pre-auth timeout and TLS failures with linger 0 as spec 01 says, amend spec 01 in the same change, and add a connections_live case.

A ban, kick or mute that times out at 2 s answers 503 but still commits, because Database::call cannot be cancelled; live.kick, live.mute and the event are then skipped (server/src/admin_api.rs:1127-1158, accounts.rs:104-106). Also, a login that commits just before a ban registers in Live afterwards (network.rs:533-539). Do not abandon a committing change (or apply kick, mute and event when it lands), register the connection before the login's DB step, and add a discord_login_live case with a stalled DB.

listener.accept().await? on the game port (server/src/network.rs:927) and on the admin port (admin_api.rs:648) ends the realm on a transient accept error (ECONNABORTED, EMFILE, ENOBUFS). Log a bounded line and continue, backing off briefly on EMFILE, ENFILE and ENOBUFS; add a unit or live test that injects an fd exhaustion.

The launcher checks Q43's https rule on the first URL only, and ureq follows up to 10 redirects, including https to http (launcher/src/net.rs:35-59, 107-124). Check every hop (or https_only for non-loopback URLs, plus a redirect limit). Require 64 lowercase hex for every artifact sha256 before it becomes a file name (install.rs:88, run.rs:173-175). launcher_live cases for an https-to-http redirect and a ../ sha.

The Redis login throttle is keyed on the full source address (server/src/network.rs:287, cache.rs:168-170), but admission buckets IPv6 by /64, so one /64 multiplies the 30/IP/min limit and the number of Discord exchanges. Key it on admission::source_key; add a test with two addresses in one /64.

The 401 ops alert re-arms on any outcome that is not a 401 rather than on success (commands.rs:265-268). REALM_REDIS and GITHUB_WORKFLOW are not validated at start (config.rs:248-273, spec 05:39). bot_live cases: /deploy force with the API down; a duration of 1ö. The n*seconds overflow wraps in release builds and can pass the <= 10y check: test both build modes.

Spec 03 test 6 and the M1 roadmap entry claim an admin_audit row with token_name for each token-authorised mutation; no code writes one. So bot kicks, bans and mutes are recorded only in Redis and stderr. Add a migration and write the row in the account change's transaction, with result idempotency per spec 03:209-217; assert it in discord_login_live; reconcile architecture.md's 'Not doing: audit log'.
